@WillAyd Here's something that's tripping me up - if I change line 332 of `pandas/core/groupby/generic.py` so it reads
```

then, if I have
```

>>> import pandas._testing as tm

>>> df = tm.makeTimeDataFrame().head()

issue_context.title: Multiple aggregations with the same name get overwritten
issue_context.body:
#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example if possible

```
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from functools import partial

df = pd.DataFrame(
    np.random.randn(1000, 3), 
    index=pd.date_range('1/1/2012', freq='S', periods=1000), 
    columns=['A', 'B', 'C']
)
dfg = df.resample('3T').agg(
    {'A': [
        partial(np.quantile, q=.9999), 
        partial(np.quantile, q=.1111),
    ]}
)
```

review_comments: can you add a comment why we have a PerformanceWarning
Generally for this, we would just silence / filter the warning. We don't specifically care that there's a warning here.

This is thrown by
```python
assert col in right
```
in `assert_frame_equal`
Do we need this branch? Is there a test that hits this?

@WillAyd Here's a test that hits it:
```
pytest pandas/tests/groupby/aggregate/test_aggregate.py::TestNamedAggregationSeries::test_no_args_raises
```

when we get here, for that test, we have:
```
-> result = Series(indexed_output[0], index=index, name=columns[0])
(Pdb) indexed_output
{}
(Pdb) index
Int64Index([0, 1], dtype='int64')
(Pdb) columns
Index([], dtype='object')
```
and so
```
result = Series(indexed_output[0], index=index, name=columns[0])
```
won't work because `columns[0]` will be out of range.
I was referring to the `result = DataFrame()` line - seems very strange to return this from this function

In the test
```
pytest pandas/tests/groupby/aggregate/test_aggregate.py::TestNamedAggregationSeries::test_no_args_raises
```
we reach this branch. Before, it would hit the "else" branch, and would raise an error because `columns[0]` would be out of range - hence, I added this extra branch.

But we can avoid ever getting here by doing a check on `results` in `_aggregate_multiple_funcs`, so I'll do that instead

@WillAyd how about returning `self.obj._constructor_expanddim()` - does that seem OK?

EDIT
I'm aware that would in practice be the same as returning an empty DataFrame, it just seems more consistent with the other return types to write it like this.
Unfortunately it looks like I'd rebased and force-pushed at the time of this review so am not sure how the code looked back then
you can type results when its created
